newsitem.title: USA: VANGUARD GROUP FOUNDER STEPPING DOWN AS CHAIRMAN.
newsitem.headline: VANGUARD GROUP FOUNDER STEPPING DOWN AS CHAIRMAN.

text.p: The Vanguard Group said Wednesday President and Chief Executive Officer John Brennan will succeed founder John Bogle as chairman of the board of the Vanguard funds and The Vanguard Group, effective January 31, 1998.
Bogle will become senior chairman and remain on the board.
As senior chairman, he will continue to provide the firm with advice and guidance on issues and projects of special interest and to speak out on mutual fund industry issues.
Bogle, 68, founded Vanguard in 1974. The Group said it now has net assets exceeding $300 billion.
Brennan, 43, joined Vanguard in 1982, was named President in 1989 and became Chief Executive Officer in February 1996.
Vanguard said its board also elected Kathleen Gubanich, Michael Miller and George Sauter as managing directors.
Gubanich joined Vanguard in 1986 and is responsible for Vanguard's Human Resources Department.

Miller joined Vanguard in 1996 and is responsible for the company's strategic planning, competitive analysis, portfolio review, new business and fund development, compliance and public relations functions, as well as quality management and corporate communications programs.

Sauter joined Vanguard in 1987 and is responsible for the firm's Core Management Group. He oversees the portfolio management of Vanguard's internally managed equity funds, including more than $82 billion invested in 18 index funds and three actively managed portfolios.
The Group noted the three were previously principals of the firm. In a related action, the board has changed the Senior Vice President title held by six other Vanguard officers to Managing Director.
